panels.proposition: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are explicitly named in Christian confession — in the Nicene Creed and in the Articles of Faith alike. Shared naming does not establish identical Trinity/Godhead ontology.
panels.historic_source: Nicene-Constantinopolitan Creed / Westminster Shorter Catechism Q4–6
panels.relationship_to_counted_predicates: Related to H04 Father, H05 Son, H34–H35 Spirit language
panels.teaching_use: Establish shared threefold God-language before discussing structural differences.
panels.caution: Shared naming does not establish identical Trinity/Godhead ontology.

panels.proposition: Historic conciliar and confessional Christianity commonly affirms one divine essence or nature shared by Father, Son, and Spirit. Do not reduce all Christian Trinitarian traditions to one philosophical theory.
panels.historic_source: Nicene Creed; Augsburg Confession I; Westminster Shorter Catechism Q4–6
panels.relationship_to_counted_predicates: H56 is the nearest counted delimiter and remains Q
panels.teaching_use: Explain why the dataset is not a complete Trinity census.
panels.caution: Do not reduce all Christian Trinitarian traditions to one philosophical theory.

panels.proposition: Restoration teaching distinguishes the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost personally and gives a distinctive embodied account of the Father and the Son. This panel is explanatory; it does not create a new A/Q/D row.
panels.historic_source: Contextual contrast, not an inherited predicate row
panels.teaching_use: Connect Godhead structure to embodiment and unity without denominator drift.

panels.proposition: Unity and distinction are shared concerns even where the metaphysical account differs. The exact meaning of divine unity must be stated tradition by tradition.
panels.historic_source: Historic Trinity language guards both distinction and unity.
panels.relationship_to_counted_predicates: H56 Neither confounding nor dividing = Q
panels.teaching_use: Teach 'unity of faith' without pretending doctrinal conformity.
panels.caution: The exact meaning of divine unity must be stated tradition by tradition.
